item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Sunday, 8 November 2026
item.description:
Stargrace introduces a WoW druid whose love of nature is complicated by clumsiness, shyness, and a hilariously disastrous acorn allergy.

Bhagpuss dives into Soulframe’s pre-alpha, curious whether Digital Extremes’ fantasy spin on Warframe can land better than classic fantasy currently does.

Shintar tries WoW Forever on US servers and finds rough sharding, ugly chat, and firsthand proof that the roach army reputation exists for a reason.

Wilhelm rounds up EVE Online’s CSM21 winners and notes how CCP’s extra picks can balance missing viewpoints—or conveniently reinforce its own.

Kelly cheers Democratic gains in the U.S. midterms, highlighting House and Senate wins plus standout races in Texas, Michigan, and Ohio.

Ramen Junkie’s weekly wrap-up is mostly TV talk, with NCIS New York disappointing, NCIS Origins delivering, and a side note about getting back into writing.

Warner sees the U.S. midterms as a welcome win, but argues Stephen Miller’s return means the real fight is only getting started.

Ghastly walks through starting a biological autumn garden, from clearing beds and mulching to companion planting carrots, garlic, lettuce, and more.

Tobold shares that he’s heading into surgery for an enlarged prostate and expects a hospital stay plus a couple weeks away from blogging.

Anarchae breaks down the real cost of being online in Canada, from discounted internet and phone plans to a laptop and NAS.

Roger sets firm boundaries for Questa, his LOTRO quest-narration tool, covering OCR fixes now and future Character and Performance voice modes.

Dave Winer celebrates BonBonWeb’s rollout, pitching Markdown plus RSS as a writer-friendly, silo-resistant way to rebuild a more open web.

item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Saturday, 7 November 2026
item.description:
Anarchae pokes through Driftwood in Divinity: Original Sin 2, finding dead fish, racist townsfolk, sneaky quests, and very little actual progress.

Aywren is thrilled that Guild Wars 1 is getting new DLC, with Afterlife bringing a dynamic dungeon, skill drafting, and more reasons to revisit Tyria.

Marc looks back at Zack & Wiki on Wii as a motion-control-friendly point-and-click adventure with big cartoon energy and unusually thoughtful design.

Zack says Life is Strange: Double Exposure smartly revisits Max Caulfield and turns the original game’s ending split into a compelling new hook.

Ellie calls The Last of Us Part II exceptional and emotionally crushing, even if its fixation on misery sometimes makes the ride harder than necessary.

Wilhelm hits level 77 in Pokemon Go, with Max Battles the real slog, and already has the XP banked for the push to 78.

Jimmy digs into Deus Ex’s launch reception, long-running mythmaking, and why its reputation needs more historical grounding than internet canon gives it.

The Friendly Necromancer earns EverQuest Legends’ Godslayer title, then wonders whether to keep grinding, jump to Enshrouded, or just heal up first.

Tobold is intrigued by MMO Simulator, a management game about running an MMORPG and watching virtual players react to your design choices.

Cristian posts a brutally short sleep log: just three hours total, split across two rough stretches before dawn.

Scopique rounds up a new Switch 2, early dungeon-crawling fun with Underkeep, and a neat web find in Spelunkr.tv.

Dave Winer unveils BonBonWeb, his Markdown-first “writers web” prototype built around replaceable parts, reader-controlled presentation, and no silos.

item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Friday, 6 November 2026
item.description:
Frostilyte uses Clair in Pokémon Silver to test low-tier anti-Dragon plans, and one weak Aurora Beam quickly makes Lance look a lot scarier.

Sey spotlights a tasty mix of indie finds, from Bibidi Bibidi! and Moomin to TANUKI, Danchi Days’ soundtrack, and the CONTINUE magazine buzz.

Juhis admits he misjudged Pokémon TCG Live’s economy, saying years later he has plenty of credits and enough cards for decks and goofy formats.

Kimimi is charmed by Hikouki de GO!’s tiny LCD cockpit, where levers, radio chatter, and lots of readouts make pocket piloting surprisingly intense.

David recaps a lively Pirate Borg opener full of pickpocketing, cursed rumors, harpies, rum treasure, and a nasty shark attack at Smuggler’s Spit.

Wilhelm says WoW Forever’s launch was a little shaky at first, but queues stayed short and layering eventually let the group actually play together.

Tipa rounds up suspicious Ankeny Kickstarter gadget campaigns, calling out AI art, steep pledge-manager fees, and products that seem to stall before shipping.

Bhagpuss spins a check on Amazon Luna into a wry meditation on memory, false recall, and why old blog posts beat trusting your brain.

Joar breaks down the retirement-to-Medicare gap, arguing COBRA, ACA timing, and deductibles need the same hard-nosed planning as any other liability.

Kelly used Google AI to build a Python script that checks Fedora release.json and emails him about new stable releases, then scheduled it with launchd.

Bruce Schneier points to early examples of LLMs finding exploitable loopholes in German law, a small preview of how AI could stress legal systems.

Axxuy turns Writing Month into a candid ramble on morning pages, Earl Grey, and the familiar struggle of wanting to write more than writing.

item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Thursday, 5 November 2026
item.description:
Anarchae’s Divinity: Original Sin 2 run hits poisoned shores, tricky voidwoken fights, and a chicken quest that turns nastier than expected.

Roger reports LOTRO private server Echoes of Angmar may be nearing the end after an online attack and the developers’ decision to retire.

Heartless mourns BioWare’s closure and the end of the next Mass Effect, calling it a sad final chapter for a once-defining RPG studio.

Ramen Junkie finds Diana the Acrobat a decent Dungeons & Dragons figure with good looks and accessories, but articulation that never quite delivers.

Margot celebrates the rise of white wolf companions, shouting out Neva, Soulframe, Okami, and other games riding the very good wolf trend.

Joar’s October gaming was all short sessions: FFXIV lost him to queues, Aion 2 stayed a side dabble, and WoW delves fit perfectly.

Shintar rounds up retail WoW highs before WoW Forever, from Brewfest chowdown wins to Mythic+ fatigue and finally seeing Venomous Abyss in LFR.

Sweetie bounced from 7’Scarlet’s spooky mystery to Dragon Quest Monsters: The Dark Prince, enjoying demos, autumn vibes, and a welcome return to Dragon Quest IV.

Wilhelm eyes the World of Warcraft Forever launch like a tourist, expecting queues, bugs, and Reddit outrage—but maybe Blizzard finally sticks the landing.

The Chronicler spotlights Wroth as a colorful but bloody area-control game with asymmetric factions, dice drafting, bots, and serious table-presence.

Warner is relieved by the Democrats’ midterm wins, but stays wary about the hard work ahead and Trump’s likely backlash.

Joel found Dune Messiah dense but gripping, praising its ominous political plotting, prophetic tension, and Paul Atreides’ burden as galactic emperor.

item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Wednesday, 4 November 2026
item.description:
Syp is ready for a full WoW Forever month, with side helpings of LOTRO and cozy hibernation energy for the rest of November.

Tipa digs Guild Wars 2’s big Vloxx dilemma but says the god-fight mechanics are a miserable slog, even if the story setup is fun.

Cliffski breaks down Ridiculous Space Battles’ tiny £915.20 budget, with stock assets and AI art/voice doing a lot of the heavy lifting.

Frostilyte recaps an October derailed by Steam Next Fest and reviews, then makes time to rave about Well Dweller’s everything-clicks appeal.

Heartless says Mistfall Hunter weirdly makes fantasy extraction plus Souls-like combat click, with tense loot runs and fights that feel worth taking.

Bhagpuss is intrigued by Silver Palace’s Victorian-anime-gacha genre blender, even while suspecting the detective angle could be the catch.

Marc looks back at the Wii’s launch by tracing Nintendo’s shaky pre-2006 position and how different the company’s fortunes feel now.

Wilhelm finds Over the Hill’s Asgard Mountain a real difficulty spike, full of icy trails, winch saves, and plenty of tumbling off cliffs.

Tobold recommends Frosthaven Digital in story mode, arguing the relaxed resting rules make its brutal card-timer tactics finally fun instead of maddening.

UltrViolet celebrates a rare good Commanders week, then wrestles with moving his AI fantasy league off ChatGPT to a local Antigravity setup.

Dave Winer celebrates Atlantis getting Frontier’s debugger back, which matters because he builds and tests code right inside it.

Cristian argues France’s proposed per-GB internet tax hits content providers first, but streaming, games, and subscription prices would likely feel it next.
